Example 8 
Carbon dioxide, CO,, is a greenhouse gas. 
a) Explain the greenhouse effect. 
b) Outline how the molecules of carbon dioxide interact with 
infrared (IR) radiation. 
Solution 
a) Greenhouse gases allow short-wavelength radiation (visible light) 
from the Sun to pass through the atmosphere. This radiation warms 
the Earth’s surface, which emits longer-wavelength (IR) radiation. 
Greenhouse gases absorb IR radiation and re-radiate it in all directions, 
so some IR radiation is returned to Earth’s surface and warms it further. 
The warm surface exchanges heat with the lower atmosphere, which 
increases the global temperature. 
b) Whena CO, molecule is excited by absorbing an IR photon, the 
C=0 bonds begin to vibrate (stretch and bend). The excited molecule 
quickly returns to its ground state by emitting an IR photon of the same 
energy in a random direction.

Biofuels 
Biofuels are produced largely from plant material, microorganisms and 
biological waste. The primary source of organic compounds used for biofuel 
production is photosynthesis, which is a form of biological fixation of carbon. 
Green plants use photosynthesis to convert carbon dioxide and water into 
glucose, C.H,,0,, and oxygen gas, through a series of redox reactions: 
6CO,(g) + 6H,0(1) - C.H ,0 (aq) + 60,(g) 
Most redox reactions involved in photosynthesis are non-spontaneous, so they 
require an external source of energy. This energy is supplied by the Sunin the 
form of visible light. Chlorophyll, a biological pigment in green plants, absorbs 
sunlight and converts it into chemical energy, which is used to drive forward

non-spontaneous reactions. Ultimately, the energy of solar radiation is utilized % 
and stored in chemical bonds of glucose. 
In turn, glucose can be converted by fermentation to other organic 
compounds, such as ethanol: 
CH O.(aq) - 2C,H,OH(aq) + 2CO,(g) 
Ethanol is more reduced than glucose because it contains less oxygen per unit 
mass. As a result, the combustion of ethanol produces almost twice as much 
energy per gram as the combustion of glucose. In addition, ethanol is a volatile 
liquid, which makes it a much better fuel than glucose. 
Combustion of ethanol and other biofuels releases carbon dioxide. However, 
these carbon emissions are largely offset by the biological carbon fixation in 
the green plants used for fuel production. Therefore, the net amount of carbon 
dioxide released to the atmosphere per kilowatt of energy obtained from 
biofuels is much lower than that for fossil fuels. 
Fossil fuels are finite resources that take millions of years to form. In contrast, 
biofuels are renewable resources that can be produced sustainably over 
a relatively short period of time (months to years). However, the industrial 
production of biofuels has ethical, economic and environmental implications, 
such as the “food versus fuel” debate, cost and sustainability (table 6).

Fuel cells 
A fuel cell converts the chemical energy of afuel directly into electrical energy. 
The fuelis continuously supplied from an external source, and oxygen gas is 
usually taken from the atmosphere, so the cell can produce electricity for as 
long as required. 
The hydrogen fuel cell (figure 8) uses hydrogen gas as the fuel, which 
undergoes oxidation on a platinum catalyst and releases electrons to the 
anode (negative electrode): 
H (g) — 2H*(aq) + 2e￾The hydrogen ions travel through the electrolyte to the cathode (positive 
electrode), where they combine with atmospheric oxygen and electrons:

evaporation.

* Entropy (S) is a measure of Entropy 
the dispersal of matter and Entropy (S) is a measure of the disorder in a system. The more predictable the 
energy ina system. states of individual particles (atoms, molecules or ions) in a system are, the 
lower the entropy of that system, and vice versa. 
In a solid lattice, all particles have fixed positions, and their movement is 
limited to vibration and rotation, so entropy values of solid substances are 
low. Liquids have higher entropies than solids because their particles have no 
fixed coordinates, and they can move in random directions with respect to 
one another. However, the particles of a liquid interact with one another, and 
the distances between adjacent particles vary only slightly, so the difference 
in entropy between solid and liquid states of the same substance is relatively 
small. In contrast, gases have very high entropy values because their particles 
move freely, the intermolecular distances vary over greater ranges, and both 
the positions and kinetic energies of individual particles are completely 
unpredictable. Therefore, for the same substance, the entropy values increase 
from solid to liquid and from liquid to gaseous state (figure 9).

Advantages:
DMFCs can be used continuously (they do not need to be recharged) while lead–acid batteries must be recharged periodically
DMFCs have higher specific energy and higher energy density than lead–acid batteries
in contrast to lead–acid batteries, DMFCs do not contain toxic lead compounds.
Disadvantages:
DMFCs are more expensive than lead–acid batteries
DMFCs typically produce lower electric current than lead–acid batteries
in contrast to lead–acid batteries, DMFCs need a constant supply of fuel
in contrast to lead–acid batteries, DMFCs use a toxic and flammable fuel (methanol)
in contrast to lead–acid batteries, DMFCs work well only when hot
in contrast to lead–acid batteries, DMFCs produce a greenhouse gas (carbon dioxide)
in contrast to lead–acid batteries, the electrodes in DMFCs can be poisoned by impurities in the fuel.
To score full marks, you need to mention any one advantage and any one disadvantage.
